replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: To solve a second order algebraic equation, first, bring all terms to one side so the equation is set to zero. Then, identify coefficients a, b, and c. Next, use the quadratic formula x = (-b ± sqrt(b² - 4ac)) / (2a) to find the roots. Finally, check your solutions by plugging them back into the original equation.

To find the stationary points of y=f(x), first differentiate f(x) to get f'(x). Then, set f'(x)=0 and solve for x to find candidate points. Next, use the second derivative f''(x) to determine if these points are minima, maxima, or points of inflection. Finally, plug the x-values back into f(x) to get the corresponding y-coordinates.
